forms.plain_english: SEC staff-generated letters to a company: comment letters on a 10-K/10-Q/8-K/registration statement, follow-ups, 'no review' notices and 'completed our review' closing letters. Posted publicly on EDGAR after the review closes.
forms.who_files_when: Filed by SEC Division of Corporation Finance (not the company). Letters ask for a response within ten business days. Public release is at least 20 business days after review completion (SEC policy; not verified from the pages fetched). Frequency for these companies: sporadic, 0-4 per year, none predictable.

companies.frequency: sporadic, roughly one review per year 2019-2024

machine_readable.format: PDF letter (filename1.pdf) plus plain-text extract (filename2.txt); accession prefix 0000000000-YY (SEC-generated, not filer-generated)
structured_fields: filing reviewed (form, fiscal year end, file number)
comment number, section heading, page reference
regulation cited (e.g. Item 303(b) Reg S-K, ASC 280-10-50-40)
SEC office (e.g. Office of Technology, Office of Trade & Services)

company.detail: AAPL 2024-03-06 letter to CFO Luca Maestri on FY2023 10-K: asked Apple to quantify Services drivers in MD&A (p.22) and to justify presenting Services as one line under ASC 280-10-50-40, with revenue breakout by type.
company.quote: (paraphrased from fetch summary; verbatim not captured)

company.detail: AAPL 2024-04-02 follow-up: asked about nature of each service (advertising vs digital content vs AppleCare), gross vs net (App Store third-party sales), customer differences, quantitative significance.
company.quote: (paraphrased)

company.detail: AAPL 2024-05-16 closing letter: staff 'completed our review' of the FY2023 10-K, Office of Technology.
company.quote: completed our review of your filing

company.detail: AMZN 2021-09-23 letter to CFO Brian Olsavsky on FY2020 10-K: four climate comments (consistency with CSR report, quantify capex/compliance cost for net-zero 2040, indirect consequences, transition risks). Ten-business-day deadline.
company.quote: Please respond to these comments within ten business days

company.detail: AMZN 2022-02-24 closing letter, no comments, Office of Trade & Services. Review ran 2021-09-23 to 2022-02-24, about 5 months across 4 letters.
company.quote: We have completed our review of your filing.

company.detail: MSFT 2024-06-17 letter on 8-K (filed 2024-01-19) and 8-K/A (2024-03-08) Item 1.05 cybersecurity incident; Microsoft replied 2024-06-28. Letter body itself not read; scope taken from the CORRESP.
company.quote: (from Microsoft response)

company.detail: MSFT 2024-05-01 UPLOAD is a 'no review' notice on an S-4 (File 333-278958): staff 'have not reviewed and will not review' it. Shows UPLOAD also carries routine administrative letters.
company.quote: have not reviewed and will not review your registration statement

executives.detail: Responding officers: Apple CFO Luca Maestri (signed 2024-03-20 response; later letters addressed to him); Amazon Worldwide Controller Shelley L. Reynolds (signed Oct 21 and Dec 7, 2021 responses) while CFO Brian Olsavsky was the addressee; Microsoft Deputy GC Keith Dolliver (signed 2024-06-28); Microsoft Asst GC Michael Pressman (S-4 addressee). Useful for an officer-role module.

growth.detail: Apple's Services line (advertising, App Store, digital content, AppleCare, cloud) was big enough that SEC probed its disaggregation; Services net sales up $7.1B FY2022 to FY2023 per Apple's response.
growth.quote: Services net sales increased $7.1 billion from fiscal year 2022 to fiscal year 2023

signals.detail: Comment themes seen: Services disaggregation/segment (AAPL), climate (AMZN), cyber 8-K Item 1.05 materiality (MSFT). Review length is a risk signal: Apple 2024-03-06 to 2024-05-16 (71 days); Amazon about 5 months.

financial_intelligence.detail: Apple used a redacted registrant-level materiality threshold to argue that a $11.0B net sales decline and $7.1B Services rise were immaterial for added MD&A detail (response letter).
financial_intelligence.quote: management did not believe further description of the change in Services net sales was necessary

products.name: Comment-letter intelligence feed (accounting-risk early warning)
products.description: Parse every UPLOAD/CORRESP pair into issues (topic, regulation cited, ask, company answer, outcome: closed with no change / agreed to revise future filings / amended). Link to the reviewed filing and to later 10-K text changes.
products.buyers: Auditors, audit committees, short-sellers, quant funds, D&O insurers, IR/disclosure counsel benchmarking peers
products.decision_supported: Which disclosure areas the SEC is pressing this year; whether a company's issue is resolved; peer benchmarking before filing
products.latency: Daily scrape of EDGAR; inherent 20+ business day SEC lag, so signal is 1-3 months behind the letter date
products.legal_notes: SEC filings are public domain; CORRESP may contain confidential-treatment redactions, never attempt to unredact

forms.suggestion: Sell a 'SEC comment-letter tracker' endpoint: per-company list of review threads with topic tags and status (open, closed with no change, committed to revise). Start with 10-K reviews only.
caveats: EDGAR filing dates on UPLOAD match the letter date (e.g. AAPL letter dated 2024-03-06 and index date 2024-03-06), so the true public release date is not on the index and the 20-business-day lag could not be measured from fetched pages
Letter body text for several letters was summarised by the fetch tool, quotes marked paraphrased where verbatim not captured
Microsoft 2024-06-17 and 2024-10-10 letters not read directly
Netflix, Google and Berkshire letters not read; only listed

forms.plain_english: The company's written responses to SEC staff comments, filed by the company or its law firm, released with the staff letters. May contain redactions under confidential treatment requests.
forms.who_files_when: Filed by the issuer (self-filed, or by a filing agent such as Donnelley 0001193125, Toppan Merrill 0001140361). Normally due ten business days after the staff letter; Apple replied in 14 days (03-06 to 03-20).

structured_fields: response to numbered staff comments (Staff comment then Response)

company.detail: Apple 2024-03-20 (Maestri): declined added quantitative Services discussion; used redacted materiality threshold; Services lines: Advertising, App Store, Digital Content, AppleCare, Cloud Services; revenue by type given supplementally, not on EDGAR.
company.quote: they all represent services delivered to Apple product customers related to Apple products

company.detail: Apple 2024-04-29 second response: analysis largely redacted; Apple said ASC 280 does not define 'similar' and that change in Services was quantitatively and qualitatively immaterial; no firm commitment to change filings. Apple also filed an intermediate 2024-04-05 response via an agent (0001140361-24-018378), not read.
company.quote: management concluded that the change in Services net sales was both quantitatively and qualitatively immaterial

company.detail: Amazon 2021-10-21 (Reynolds): refused to mirror CSR-report climate detail; said no material climate capex to date; would only 'monitor and evaluate'.
company.quote: we will continue to monitor and evaluate our climate-related disclosures

company.detail: Amazon 2021-12-07: Climate Pledge capex about $250M in 2020; FERC compliance cost under $1M; renewable/carbon reporting staff under $10M; 'Climate Pledge Friendly' badge launched Sept 2020, over 200,000 products by Oct 2021; committed that 2021 10-K would add a risk statement on failing Climate Pledge goals.
company.quote: we do not currently view these as material trends

company.detail: Microsoft 2024-06-28 (Dolliver): Jan 12 2024 detection of nation-state actor access to employee email from late Nov 2023; filed 8-K Item 1.05 although not judged material, citing SEC guidance to resolve doubt toward disclosure; said reputational harm not reasonably likely material; would file 8-K/A if that changed.
company.quote: do not believe the harm to our reputation and customer relationships is reasonably likely to have a material impact

executives.detail: Keith Dolliver (Microsoft Deputy GC and Corporate Secretary) signs SEC correspondence; Shelley Reynolds (Amazon VP, Worldwide Controller) signs for Amazon.

growth.detail: Amazon: 'Climate Pledge Friendly' covered over 200,000 products by October 2021.

signals.detail: Microsoft Item 1.05 cyber 8-K questioned by SEC for filing under 1.05 without a materiality finding; SEC staff statement of 2024-05-21 acknowledged.

financial_intelligence.detail: Apple FY2023 total net sales fell $11.0B and Services rose $7.1B, both stated below Apple's internal materiality threshold (amount redacted).

products.name: Response-quality and outcome scoring

forms.plain_english: SEC order granting a company's request to keep parts of a filed exhibit (typically material contracts) confidential, usually for a stated number of years. The order names the filing and exhibit and an expiry date.
forms.who_files_when: Issued by the SEC; appears under the company CIK. Rare. Accession prefix 9999999997.

machine_readable.format: PDF (uuencoded in the .txt) with SGML header

company.detail: Amazon CT order accession 9999999997-17-006496 under file 000-22513, received 2017-05-24, filed 2017-05-26. Body (covered exhibit, expiry) not decodable via the fetch tool.
company.quote: n/a

products.description: Track CT orders and expiry dates, since terms become public once confidentiality ends.
products.decision_supported: When hidden contract terms may surface

forms.suggestion: Not a standalone product; at most a field on the company event feed. Note the SEC largely moved CT handling to Rule 24b-2 redactions, so volume is tiny.

forms.plain_english: Specialized Disclosure report. Two uses: conflict minerals (Rule 13p-1; tin, tantalum, tungsten, gold from DRC and adjoining countries) with Exhibit 1.01 Conflict Minerals Report, and resource extraction payments to governments (Rule 13q-1) with an XBRL exhibit.
forms.who_files_when: Conflict minerals due 31 May each year for the prior calendar year; resource extraction payments due 270 days after fiscal year end (about late September for December year-ends). Annual.

companies.frequency: annual resource extraction (Sept) plus conflict minerals (May, latest 2026-05-22 0001193125-26-236936, not read)

machine_readable.format: HTML main doc; Ex-1.01 HTML (conflict minerals); Ex-2.01 inline XBRL plus XML instance and xsd (BRK resource extraction, taxonomy brka-20251231.xsd)
structured_fields: payment: project ID, country, payee government, payment type, amount, currency, subnational jurisdiction, business segment, resource, extraction method

company.detail: Apple FY2025 SD (period Jan 1-Dec 31 2025, signed 2026-05-28) is a short cover report; no smelter counts or names in it, points to apple.com/supply-chain. 3TG may originate in Covered Countries.
company.quote: Apple believes that 3TG contained in our products may have originated from the Covered Countries.

company.detail: Apple 2025 filing (CY2024) Ex-1.01: 234 smelters and refiners identified; 100% in third-party audit; 203 removed cumulatively since 2009; Annex I lists 78 origin countries; suppliers told in June 2024 to stop sourcing 3TG from DRC and Rwanda; Russia flagged for sanctions. No smelter-by-name list in the SEC filing (on Apple's website).
company.quote: we have identified a total of 234 smelters and refiners that processed 3TG in our supply chain during 2024.

company.detail: Microsoft Ex-1.01 (2026): 79 direct suppliers surveyed, 100% response; 266 eligible SORs; 220 (82.7%) Conformant, 14 Non-Conformant, 6 Active; 226 (84.9%) in audit; 31 SORs sourced from Covered Countries, all Conformant. Scope: Surface, Xbox, HoloLens, Nuance devices. Appendix A: mineral, name, country (e.g. Gold, Argor-Heraeus S.A., Switzerland).
company.quote: 31 SORs sourced from Covered Countries, of which 31 (100%) were Conformant.

company.detail: Amazon Ex-1.01 (CY2025): Annex A lists roughly 500 facilities (fetch-tool estimate), columns Mineral/Name/Country, includes one DRC tin facility, Mining Minerals Resources SARL; Amazon says it cannot confirm which facilities serve it. No supplier counts or response rate.
company.quote: we are unable to validate the accuracy of the list in Annex A.

company.quote: All amounts reported in the table below relate to natural gas resources within Northern Powergrid

company.quote: below the de minimis threshold under Rule 13q-1

forms.plain_english: Short notice under Section 13(r) of the Exchange Act (Iran Threat Reduction Act s.219) telling the SEC that the company has put required disclosure of Iran/sanctions-related activity in its 10-K or 10-Q. The notice does not carry the details.
forms.who_files_when: Filed with the periodic report that contains the 13(r) disclosure, often same day or next. Companies file it for the quarter containing the activity, and again in the 10-K if it relates to previously disclosed matters.

companies.frequency: 8 notices 2022-10 to 2026-02, roughly twice a year (Oct and Feb)

structured_fields: report form and filing date it points to

company.quote: limited and lawful dealings with the Russian Federal Security Service
